question.value: What is the water vapor abundance in embedded Class I Keplerian disks, from spatially resolved H2 18O line observations?

evidence.quote: We aim to determine the water abundance in embedded Keplerian disks through spatially-resolved observations of H$_2^{18}$O lines
(project code: 2013.1.00448.S; PI: M. Persson)
The observations in Band 8 were carried out with 35 antennas under good weather conditions

findings_qualitative.value: No H2 18O emission detected toward any of the five Class I objects

evidence.quote: No H$_2^{18}$O emission is detected toward any of our five Class I disks.

findings_qualitative.value: Class I water column density upper limits are at least two orders of magnitude lower than Class 0 disk-like structures

evidence.quote: Upper limits to the water vapor column densities in Class I disks are at least two orders magnitude lower than values found in Class 0 disk-like structures.

claims.hypothesis: Do Class I disks have abundant warm water vapor?
claims.experiment: H2 18O 203 and 390 GHz observations of five Class I objects
claims.finding: Water vapor is not abundant in warm Class I envelopes/disks on 100 au scales

evidence.quote: The upper limits imply a disk-averaged water abundance of $\lesssim \! 10^{-6}$

claims.experiment: Power-law disk emission models with small and large grains
claims.result: Large grains reduce the emitting region; line optically thick and beam diluted
claims.finding: Large dust grains plausibly suppress emission, consistent with hidden water inside 10 au

evidence.quote: dust grain evolution in young disks provides the most plausible explanation for the weak water lines toward Class I disks.

why_this_method.value: Same column-density method as Class 0 studies for comparison

evidence.quote: In order to compare with previous water detections toward Class 0 objects (cite: jorgensen10a; persson12), a similar approach is adopted

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Steeper surface density slope (R^-1.75) rejected as solution

evidence.quote: Thus, a steeper power-law profile is not the solution.

limitations_admitted.value: GSS30 observed with incorrect phase center at ~10% of primary beam, giving much lower sensitivity

evidence.quote: the observations toward the GSS30 system used an incorrect phase center such that the objects are located $\sim$12$''$ away

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits depend on assumed 1 km/s Gaussian line width and T_ex = 200 K
Disk masses from 750 um dust likely lower limits (optically thick)
Large-grain explanation not directly tested with data
